¿Tu cachorro sale corriendo apenas abres la puerta? Este comportamiento se trabaja con autocontrol. La idea es enseñarle que lanzarse hacia afuera no hace que la puerta se abra ni que pueda salir más rápido. Haz el ejercicio así: abre la puerta lentamente. Si tu cachorro intenta salir, ciérrala de inmediato. Repite varias veces. Cuando se quede quieto, reconoce ese momento, celebra que lo hizo bien y luego dale una señal clara para salir. Importante: esto no se aprende en una sola sesión. La clave está en aprovechar cada vez que vas a salir de la casa para practicarlo como parte de la rutina. Con suficientes repeticiones, tu perro empieza a entender el comportamiento correcto: esperar primero y salir solo cuando tú se lo indiques. La puerta no debe ser una invitación a salir corriendo. Debe ser una oportunidad para practicar calma, paciencia y autocontrol. #cachorros #perritos #educacioncanina #adiestramientocanino #australianshepherd

Korean Popcorn Chicken 🍿🐔 Ingredients Chicken: • 1.1 lb (500 g) boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces • 1 egg • ½ tsp salt • ½ tsp black pepper • 1 tsp garlic powder • ½ tsp ginger powder • ½ tsp chicken bouillon • 5 tbsp cornstarch • 3 tbsp all-purpose flour Sauce: • 1.5 tbsp butter • 2 garlic cloves, minced • 1.5 tbsp gochujang • 3 tbsp ketchup • 1 tbsp soy sauce • 2 tbsp light brown sugar • 1 tbsp honey • 2 tsp rice vinegar • 1 tsp sesame oil Garnish: • Toasted sesame seeds • Sliced green onions Instructions: 1. Season the chicken with the egg, salt, black pepper, garlic powder, ginger powder, and chicken bouillon. Mix well and let rest for 10 minutes. 2. Add the cornstarch and flour, then toss until evenly coated. 3. Fry at 320–330°F (160–165°C) until cooked through. Let rest for 2–3 minutes. 4. Fry again at 355°F (180°C) until golden and crispy. 5. Melt the butter and saute the garlic until fragrant. 6. Add the gochujang, ketchup, soy sauce, light brown sugar, honey, rice vinegar, and sesame oil. Cook until glossy. 7. Toss the chicken in the sauce until evenly coated. 8. Garnish with toasted sesame seeds and sliced green onions. #chickenrecipes #koreanfood #popcorn #chicken #fyp

thick bakery style chocolate chip cookies🍪🍫 Ingredients: 170g (3/4 cup) unsalted butter, cold and cubed 150g (3/4 cup) brown sugar 70g (1/3 cup) granulated sugar 1 egg + 1 egg yolk 2 tsp vanilla 300g (2 1/2 cups) all purpose flour 1 tbsp cornstarch 1/2 tsp baking soda 1/4 tsp baking powder 3/4 tsp salt 250g (1 1/2 cups) chocolate chips  Flakey sea salt (optional) Instructions:  1. In a large bowl, combine the butter, brown sugar, and white sugar. Mix until smooth and well combined. Do not cream. 2. Add the egg, egg yolk, and vanilla, then mix until fully incorporated. 3. Add the dry ingredients (flour, cornstarch, baking powder, baking soda, and salt) and fold until just combined. 4. Fold in the chocolate chips or chunks until evenly distributed. Do not overmix. 5. Divide the dough into 150g portions and shape each into a rough ball. 6. Place the dough balls on a lined tray, cover, and refrigerate for at least 1 hour or overnight. 7. Bake in a preheated 190°C (375°F) oven for 13-16 minutes, or until the edges are golden brown and the centers are still slightly soft. 8. Allow the cookies to cool on the baking tray for a few minutes, then transfer to a wire rack. If desired, sprinkle with flaky sea salt and let cool for about 15 minutes before serving. Enjoy! Note: This recipe made 6 cookies weighing 150g each and 1 cookie weighing 100g🍪🤎 #baking #cookies #chocolatechipcookies #Recipe #nyccookies

“Dog lovers” vs dog lovers when it comes to greeting dogs! ETA: “dog lovers” could also be replaced with “uniformed, uneducated, and/or inconsiderate dog lovers” vs “informed, educated, and considerate dog lovers” if that makes you more comfortable 🫶 One of my biggest pet peeves is people baby talking to my dog and pretending like I’m interrupting? Bizarre! And in case you didn’t know because it’s something that’s been so normalized, putting your hands in dogs’ faces is unsafe. Dogs don’t need to sniff you up close like that and it’s putting unneeded pressure on them (often leading to bites). The best way to greet a dog is calm, neutral, and honestly just ignoring them. If you want to say hi to a dog, ask the owner first. Try to make yourself small by turning to the side and crouching. Allow the dog to approach you first. Some dogs are super friendly and love people! This doesn’t mean it’s ok to pet or approach without asking their handler! The safest way to greet any dog is by admiring from afar. Admittedly, if I know someone’s dog well, I might be a bit of the former “dog lover” and be excitedly greeting them 😂 It’s different when you know the dog! The easiest Korean meal I make for guests Samgyeopsal Kimchi Jjim (삼겹살 김치찜) 🧡 Ingredients  500 g (1.1 lb) aged kimchi 1 kg (2.2 lb) pork belly 💙 Directions  1. Add the kimchi and pork belly to a pot. Pour in enough water to just cover the ingredients. 2. Bring to a boil, then reduce to medium heat and simmer for 40–60 minutes. 💡 Tips - Don't use fresh kimchi! This dish only works with well-fermented (aged) kimchi. If you're buying kimchi from the store, look for "aged" or "fermented" on the label. If you can only find regular kimchi, let it ferment at room temperature for about 2 days or in the refrigerator for about 5 days before using it. - If your kimchi is too sour, add 1 tbsp sugar. If it's not sour enough, add 1 tbsp vinegar. - You can use any cut of pork, but fattier cuts work best because the rendered fat adds richness to the broth and kimchi. I recommend pork belly or pork shoulder. - I also added 1 tbsp plum syrup and ½ tbsp doenjang (Korean soybean paste). These are completely optional, but they help reduce any pork odor and add extra umami. Since kimchi is already seasoned with garlic, chili peppers, and other aromatics, you don't need any additional seasoning to make this dish delicious. 🔖 Save this recipe for your next meal  🥰 Like, follow & comment if you enjoyed  .  .  . .  . . #k#koreanfoode#EasyRecipesc#comfortfoodkimchi #samgyupsal
